title: Length Word Problems and Number Lines
standard_text: 2.9C represent whole numbers as distances from any given location on a number line; 2.9E determine a solution to a problem involving length, including estimating lengths
meta_desc: Free Grade 2 length word problem worksheets for Texas TEKS 2.9C and 2.9E: lengths and jumps on a number line, joining, comparing and unknown lengths. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Join lengths: add. Cut off or compare: subtract.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Lengths are numbers, so you can add and subtract them.
  • Joining two pieces: add. Cutting off or comparing: subtract.
  • On a number line, each jump is a distance from one number to another.
  • Keep the same unit: inches with inches, meters with meters.

Examples

Example

A ribbon is 45 cm. Ava cuts off 18 cm.

45 − 18

Answer: 27 cm

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Adding when you should subtractCut off or how much longer means subtract.
Mixing unitsUse the same unit for every length.
Counting the start as a jumpCount the spaces you jump over.

faq.a: Determine a solution to a problem involving length, including estimating lengths.
Represent whole numbers as distances from any given location on a number line.

faq.q: How do I compare two lengths?
faq.a: Subtract the shorter length from the longer one.
Yes. An estimate helps you check your answer.

items.q: Each small space is 1. What number is at the red dot?
items.e: Find the big mark just before the dot: 30. Count the spaces after it, not the marks: 31, 32, 33, 34, 35, 36, 37. 30 + 7 = 37. (It is also 3 before 40.)

items.q: Each small space is 1. What number is at the red dot?
items.e: Find the big mark just before the dot: 70. Count the spaces after it, not the marks: 71, 72, 73, 74. 70 + 4 = 74. (It is also 6 before 80.)

items.q: Each small space is 1. What number is at the red dot?
items.e: Find the big mark just before the dot: 20. Count the spaces after it, not the marks: 21, 22, 23, 24, 25, 26, 27, 28. 20 + 8 = 28. (It is also 2 before 30.)

items.q: Each small space is 1. What number is at the red dot?
items.e: Find the big mark just before the dot: 40. Count the spaces after it, not the marks: 41, 42, 43, 44, 45, 46. 40 + 6 = 46. (It is also 4 before 50.)

items.q: Each small space is 1. What number is at the red dot?
items.e: Find the big mark just before the dot: 80. Count the spaces after it, not the marks: 81, 82, 83. 80 + 3 = 83. (It is also 2 before 85.)

items.q: Each small space is 1. What number is at the red dot?
items.e: Find the big mark just before the dot: 30. Count the spaces after it, not the marks: 31, 32. 30 + 2 = 32. (It is also 3 before 35.)

items.q: Each small space is 1. What number is at the red dot?
items.e: Find the big mark just before the dot: 10. Count the spaces after it, not the marks: 11, 12, 13. 10 + 3 = 13. (It is also 2 before 15.)

items.q: The number line is marked in centimeters. How long is the crayon?
items.e: The crayon starts at 0 and ends at 9. Count the spaces, not the marks: there are 9 spaces. Each space is 1 centimeter, so it is 9 centimeters long.

items.q: The number line is marked in centimeters. How long is the caterpillar?
items.e: The caterpillar starts at 0 and ends at 5. Count the spaces, not the marks: there are 5 spaces. Each space is 1 centimeter, so it is 5 centimeters long.

items.q: The number line is marked in centimeters. How long is the leaf?
items.e: The leaf starts at 0 and ends at 8. Count the spaces, not the marks: there are 8 spaces. Each space is 1 centimeter, so it is 8 centimeters long.

items.q: The number line is marked in centimeters. How long is the ribbon?
items.e: The ribbon starts at 0 and ends at 13. Count the spaces, not the marks: there are 13 spaces. Each space is 1 centimeter, so it is 13 centimeters long.

items.q: The number line is marked in inches. How long is the pencil?
items.e: The pencil starts at 0 and ends at 7. Count the spaces, not the marks: there are 7 spaces. Each space is 1 inch, so it is 7 inches long.

items.q: The number line is marked in inches. How long is the craft stick?
items.e: The craft stick starts at 0 and ends at 6. Count the spaces, not the marks: there are 6 spaces. Each space is 1 inch, so it is 6 inches long.

items.q: The number line is marked in inches. How long is the paper strip?
items.e: The paper strip starts at 0 and ends at 9. Count the spaces, not the marks: there are 9 spaces. Each space is 1 inch, so it is 9 inches long.

items.q: The number line is marked in centimeters. How long is the eraser?
items.e: The eraser does not start at 0. It goes from 4 to 9. Subtract: 9 − 4 = 5. Or count the spaces from 4 to 9: 5. Answer: 5 centimeters.

items.q: The number line is marked in centimeters. How long is the nail?
items.e: The nail does not start at 0. It goes from 3 to 10. Subtract: 10 − 3 = 7. Or count the spaces from 3 to 10: 7. Answer: 7 centimeters.

items.q: The number line is marked in centimeters. How long is the paper strip?
items.e: The paper strip does not start at 0. It goes from 5 to 14. Subtract: 14 − 5 = 9. Or count the spaces from 5 to 14: 9. Answer: 9 centimeters.

items.q: The number line is marked in centimeters. How long is the pencil?
items.e: The pencil does not start at 0. It goes from 2 to 15. Subtract: 15 − 2 = 13. Or count the spaces from 2 to 15: 13. Answer: 13 centimeters.

items.q: The number line is marked in inches. How long is the ribbon?
items.e: The ribbon does not start at 0. It goes from 3 to 8. Subtract: 8 − 3 = 5. Or count the spaces from 3 to 8: 5. Answer: 5 inches.

items.q: The number line is marked in inches. How long is the crayon?
items.e: The crayon does not start at 0. It goes from 2 to 6. Subtract: 6 − 2 = 4. Or count the spaces from 2 to 6: 4. Answer: 4 inches.

items.q: Start at 45. Jump 20 to the right. Where do you land?
items.e: Moving right adds. Start at 45 and move 20 spaces: 45 + 20 = ☐. 45 + 20 = 65.

items.q: Start at 23. Jump 30 to the right. Where do you land?
items.e: Moving right adds. Start at 23 and move 30 spaces: 23 + 30 = ☐. 23 + 30 = 53.

items.q: Start at 58. Jump 14 to the right. Where do you land?
items.e: Moving right adds. Start at 58 and move 14 spaces: 58 + 14 = ☐. 58 + 10 = 68. Then 68 + 4 = 72.

items.q: Start at 36. Jump 25 to the right. Where do you land?
items.e: Moving right adds. Start at 36 and move 25 spaces: 36 + 25 = ☐. 36 + 20 = 56. Then 56 + 5 = 61.

items.q: Start at 17. Jump 18 to the right. Where do you land?
items.e: Moving right adds. Start at 17 and move 18 spaces: 17 + 18 = ☐. 17 + 10 = 27. Then 27 + 8 = 35.

items.q: Start at 64. Jump 27 to the right. Where do you land?
items.e: Moving right adds. Start at 64 and move 27 spaces: 64 + 27 = ☐. 64 + 20 = 84. Then 84 + 7 = 91.

items.q: Start at 72. Jump 30 to the left. Where do you land?
items.e: Moving left subtracts. Start at 72 and move back 30 spaces: 72 − 30 = ☐. 72 − 30 = 42.

items.q: Start at 55. Jump 16 to the left. Where do you land?
items.e: Moving left subtracts. Start at 55 and move back 16 spaces: 55 − 16 = ☐. 55 − 10 = 45. Then 45 − 6 = 39.

items.q: Start at 81. Jump 25 to the left. Where do you land?
items.e: Moving left subtracts. Start at 81 and move back 25 spaces: 81 − 25 = ☐. 81 − 20 = 61. Then 61 − 5 = 56.

items.q: Start at 46. Jump 19 to the left. Where do you land?
items.e: Moving left subtracts. Start at 46 and move back 19 spaces: 46 − 19 = ☐. 46 − 10 = 36. Then 36 − 9 = 27.

items.q: Start at 90. Jump 37 to the left. Where do you land?
items.e: Moving left subtracts. Start at 90 and move back 37 spaces: 90 − 37 = ☐. 90 − 30 = 60. Then 60 − 7 = 53.

items.q: How long is the jump from 34 to 52?
items.e: Count up from 34 to 52, or subtract: 52 − 34 = 18. Check: 34 + 18 = 52. Count the spaces, not the marks.

items.q: How long is the jump from 48 to 75?
items.e: Count up from 48 to 75, or subtract: 75 − 48 = 27. Check: 48 + 27 = 75. Count the spaces, not the marks.

items.q: How long is the jump from 26 to 41?
items.e: Count up from 26 to 41, or subtract: 41 − 26 = 15. Check: 26 + 15 = 41. Count the spaces, not the marks.

items.q: How long is the jump from 57 to 83?
items.e: Count up from 57 to 83, or subtract: 83 − 57 = 26. Check: 57 + 26 = 83. Count the spaces, not the marks.

items.q: Which equation does the number line show?
items.e: The jumps are +20 and +5. Together they make 25. Start at 30 and add 25: 30 + 25 = 55.

items.q: Which equation does the number line show?
items.e: The jumps are +20 and +8. Together they make 28. Start at 43 and add 28: 43 + 28 = 71.

items.q: Which equation does the number line show?
items.e: Both jumps go left, so subtract. −20 and −6 make −26: 74 − 26 = 48.

items.q: Which number line shows 30 + 25?
items.e: Number line A starts at 30 and jumps 25 to the right, to 55. 30 + 25 = 55.

items.q: Which number line shows 62 − 24?
items.e: Number line B starts at 62 and jumps 24 to the left, to 38. 62 − 24 = 38.

items.q: Ms. Park hangs two banners end to end. One banner is 16 feet long. The other is 13 feet long. Which equation matches the story?
items.e: The two lengths are put together, so add: 16 + 13 = ☐. 16 + 13 = 29, so the total is 29 feet.

items.q: The class paints a red line 37 meters long on the playground. Then they paint a blue line 26 meters long at the end of it. Which equation matches the story?
items.e: The two lengths are put together, so add: 37 + 26 = ☐. 37 + 26 = 63, so the total is 63 meters.

items.q: Two rugs lie end to end in a hallway. One rug is 9 feet long. The other rug is 11 feet long. Which equation matches the story?
items.e: The two lengths are put together, so add: 9 + 11 = ☐. 9 + 11 = 20, so the total is 20 feet.

items.q: Ximena lays a pencil and a crayon end to end. The pencil is 17 centimeters long. The crayon is 8 centimeters long. How long are they together?
items.e: The lengths are put together, so add: 17 + 8 = ☐. 17 + 8 = 25. (7 + 8 ones make a new ten.) Answer: 25 centimeters.

items.q: A worm crawled 21 centimeters. Then it crawled 17 centimeters more. How far did the worm crawl in all?
items.e: The lengths are put together, so add: 21 + 17 = ☐. 21 + 10 = 31. Then 31 + 7 = 38. Answer: 38 centimeters.

items.q: Josiah built a block tower 28 centimeters tall. Then he added blocks to make it 15 centimeters taller. How tall is the tower now?
items.e: The lengths are put together, so add: 28 + 15 = ☐. 28 + 10 = 38. Then 38 + 5 = 43. (8 + 5 ones make a new ten.) Answer: 43 centimeters.

items.q: Aaliyah has a red ribbon 18 centimeters long and a blue ribbon 39 centimeters long. She tapes them end to end. How long is the new ribbon?
items.e: The lengths are put together, so add: 18 + 39 = ☐. 18 + 30 = 48. Then 48 + 9 = 57. (8 + 9 ones make a new ten.) Answer: 57 centimeters.

items.q: A garden fence has two parts. One part is 29 feet long. The other part is 31 feet long. How long is the whole fence?
items.e: The lengths are put together, so add: 29 + 31 = ☐. 29 + 30 = 59. Then 59 + 1 = 60. (9 + 1 ones make a new ten.) Answer: 60 feet.

items.q: Emma knit a scarf 31 inches long. Then she knit 22 more inches. How long is the scarf now?
items.e: The lengths are put together, so add: 31 + 22 = ☐. 31 + 20 = 51. Then 51 + 2 = 53. Answer: 53 inches.

items.q: Gabriel rides his bike 43 meters to a friend's house. Then he rides 39 meters to school. How far does Gabriel ride in all?
items.e: The lengths are put together, so add: 43 + 39 = ☐. 43 + 30 = 73. Then 73 + 9 = 82. (3 + 9 ones make a new ten.) Answer: 82 meters.

items.q: A paper chain is 22 feet long. The class makes 19 more feet of chain. How long is the chain now?
items.e: The lengths are put together, so add: 22 + 19 = ☐. 22 + 10 = 32. Then 32 + 9 = 41. (2 + 9 ones make a new ten.) Answer: 41 feet.

items.q: Diego walks 24 meters to the corner. Then he walks 37 meters to the park. How far does he walk in all?
items.e: The lengths are put together, so add: 24 + 37 = ☐. 24 + 30 = 54. Then 54 + 7 = 61. (4 + 7 ones make a new ten.) Answer: 61 meters.

items.q: A bookshelf is 25 inches long. Camila puts a second bookshelf 22 inches long next to it, end to end. How long are the two shelves together?
items.e: The lengths are put together, so add: 25 + 22 = ☐. 25 + 20 = 45. Then 45 + 2 = 47. Answer: 47 inches.

items.q: A bean plant was 36 centimeters tall. It grew 16 centimeters this month. How tall is the bean plant now?
items.e: The lengths are put together, so add: 36 + 16 = ☐. 36 + 10 = 46. Then 46 + 6 = 52. (6 + 6 ones make a new ten.) Answer: 52 centimeters.

items.q: Isaac swam 44 meters. Then he swam 29 more meters. How far did Isaac swim in all?
items.e: The lengths are put together, so add: 44 + 29 = ☐. 44 + 20 = 64. Then 64 + 9 = 73. (4 + 9 ones make a new ten.) Answer: 73 meters.

items.q: Dad puts two boards end to end. One board is 48 inches long. The other board is 42 inches long. How long are the two boards together?
items.e: The lengths are put together, so add: 48 + 42 = ☐. 48 + 40 = 88. Then 88 + 2 = 90. (8 + 2 ones make a new ten.) Answer: 90 inches.

items.q: A sunflower was 43 inches tall. Then it grew 26 more inches. How tall is the sunflower now?
items.e: The lengths are put together, so add: 43 + 26 = ☐. 43 + 20 = 63. Then 63 + 6 = 69. Answer: 69 inches.

items.q: A toy train has three cars. The cars are 14 centimeters, 17 centimeters and 19 centimeters long. How long is the train?
items.e: Add all three lengths: 14 + 17 + 19 = ☐. First 14 + 17 = 31. Then 31 + 19 = 50. Answer: 50 centimeters.

items.q: A trail has three parts. They are 19 meters, 17 meters and 23 meters long. How long is the whole trail?
items.e: Add all three lengths: 19 + 17 + 23 = ☐. First 19 + 17 = 36. Then 36 + 23 = 59. Answer: 59 meters.

items.q: Valeria tapes three paper strips end to end. They are 22 inches, 15 inches and 18 inches long. How long is the long strip?
items.e: Add all three lengths: 22 + 15 + 18 = ☐. First 22 + 15 = 37. Then 37 + 18 = 55. Answer: 55 inches.

items.q: A rope is 55 centimeters long. Carlos cuts off 31 centimeters. How long is the rope now?
items.e: Part of the length is taken away, so subtract: 55 − 31 = ☐. 55 − 30 = 25. Then 25 − 1 = 24. Check: 24 + 31 = 55. Answer: 24 centimeters.

items.q: A roll of paper is 44 feet long. Sofia cuts off 18 feet for a class poster. How long is the roll now?
items.e: Part of the length is taken away, so subtract: 44 − 18 = ☐. 44 − 10 = 34. Then 34 − 8 = 26. Check: 26 + 18 = 44. Answer: 26 feet.

items.q: A string is 51 centimeters long. Zoe uses 37 centimeters to make a necklace. How much string is left?
items.e: Part of the length is taken away, so subtract: 51 − 37 = ☐. 51 − 30 = 21. Then 21 − 7 = 14. Check: 14 + 37 = 51. Answer: 14 centimeters.

items.q: Isaac has to walk 91 meters to the library. He has walked 48 meters so far. How much farther does he have to walk?
items.e: You know the whole way and the part already walked. Subtract to find the part still to go: 91 − 48 = ☐. 91 − 40 = 51. Then 51 − 8 = 43. Check: 43 + 48 = 91. Answer: 43 meters.

items.q: A board is 49 inches long. Dad saws off 34 inches. How long is the board now?
items.e: Part of the length is taken away, so subtract: 49 − 34 = ☐. 49 − 30 = 19. Then 19 − 4 = 15. Check: 15 + 34 = 49. Answer: 15 inches.

items.q: A candle was 35 centimeters tall. It burned down 9 centimeters. How tall is the candle now?
items.e: Part of the length is taken away, so subtract: 35 − 9 = ☐. 35 − 9 = 26. Check: 26 + 9 = 35. Answer: 26 centimeters.

items.q: A garden hose is 61 feet long. A piece 18 feet long is cut off. How long is the hose now?
items.e: Part of the length is taken away, so subtract: 61 − 18 = ☐. 61 − 10 = 51. Then 51 − 8 = 43. Check: 43 + 18 = 61. Answer: 43 feet.

items.q: A roll of tape had 42 feet of tape. The class used 24 feet. How many feet of tape are left?
items.e: Part of the length is taken away, so subtract: 42 − 24 = ☐. 42 − 20 = 22. Then 22 − 4 = 18. Check: 18 + 24 = 42. Answer: 18 feet.

items.q: A ribbon is 48 inches long. Noah cuts off 17 inches to make a bow. How much ribbon is left?
items.e: Part of the length is taken away, so subtract: 48 − 17 = ☐. 48 − 10 = 38. Then 38 − 7 = 31. Check: 31 + 17 = 48. Answer: 31 inches.

items.q: A race is 84 meters long. Grace has run 28 meters. How many more meters does she need to run?
items.e: You know the whole race and the part already run. Subtract to find the part still to run: 84 − 28 = ☐. 84 − 20 = 64. Then 64 − 8 = 56. Check: 56 + 28 = 84. Answer: 56 meters.

items.q: The big pool is 25 meters long. The small pool is 8 meters long. How much shorter is the small pool?
items.e: To compare, find the difference. Subtract the shorter length from the longer one: 25 − 8 = ☐. 25 − 8 = 17. Check: 8 + 17 = 25. Answer: 17 meters. “How much shorter” is the same difference.

items.q: Marcus is 53 inches tall. Gabriel is 45 inches tall. How much taller is Marcus than Gabriel?
items.e: To compare, find the difference. Subtract the shorter length from the longer one: 53 − 45 = ☐. 53 − 40 = 13. Then 13 − 5 = 8. Check: 45 + 8 = 53. Answer: 8 inches.

items.q: A school bus is 39 feet long. It is 24 feet longer than a van. How long is the van?
items.e: The word “longer” is in the story, but the van is the shorter one, so subtract: 39 − 24 = ☐. 39 − 20 = 19. Then 19 − 4 = 15. Answer: 15 feet.

items.q: Elijah's paper airplane flew 25 feet. Jayden's plane flew 11 feet farther. How far did Jayden's plane fly?
items.e: Jayden's plane flew farther, so add: 25 + 11 = ☐. 25 + 10 = 35. Then 35 + 1 = 36. Answer: 36 feet.

items.q: A green toy snake is 52 centimeters long. A red toy snake is 29 centimeters long. How much longer is the green snake?
items.e: To compare, find the difference. Subtract the shorter length from the longer one: 52 − 29 = ☐. 52 − 20 = 32. Then 32 − 9 = 23. Check: 29 + 23 = 52. Answer: 23 centimeters.

items.q: A sunflower is 65 inches tall. A tulip is 17 inches tall. How much shorter is the tulip than the sunflower?
items.e: To compare, find the difference. Subtract the shorter length from the longer one: 65 − 17 = ☐. 65 − 10 = 55. Then 55 − 7 = 48. Check: 17 + 48 = 65. Answer: 48 inches. “How much shorter” is the same difference.

items.q: Liam jumped 52 inches. Caleb jumped 27 inches. How much farther did Liam jump than Caleb?
items.e: To compare, find the difference. Subtract the shorter length from the longer one: 52 − 27 = ☐. 52 − 20 = 32. Then 32 − 7 = 25. Check: 27 + 25 = 52. Answer: 25 inches.

items.q: A tree is 34 feet tall. A fence is 7 feet tall. How much taller is the tree than the fence?
items.e: To compare, find the difference. Subtract the shorter length from the longer one: 34 − 7 = ☐. 34 − 7 = 27. Check: 7 + 27 = 34. Answer: 27 feet.

items.q: A blue ribbon is 58 centimeters long. A red ribbon is 23 centimeters shorter than the blue ribbon. How long is the red ribbon?
items.e: The red ribbon is shorter, so subtract: 58 − 23 = ☐. 58 − 20 = 38. Then 38 − 3 = 35. Answer: 35 centimeters.

items.q: A desk is 27 inches tall. It is 34 inches shorter than a bookshelf. How tall is the bookshelf?
items.e: The word “shorter” is in the story, but the bookshelf is the taller one, so add: 27 + 34 = ☐. 27 + 30 = 57. Then 57 + 4 = 61. Answer: 61 inches.

items.q: A ribbon was some inches long. Lucia cut off 18 inches. Now the ribbon is 46 inches long. How long was it at first?
items.e: The start is unknown: ☐ − 18 = 46. Put the cut piece back: 46 + 18 = 64. Answer: 64 inches.

items.q: A plant grew 16 centimeters this month. Now it is 53 centimeters tall. How tall was it at the start of the month?
items.e: The start is unknown: ☐ + 16 = 53. Take away what it grew: 53 − 16 = 37. Answer: 37 centimeters.

items.q: A bean plant was 28 centimeters tall. It grew some more. Now it is 45 centimeters tall. How many centimeters did it grow?
items.e: The change is unknown: 28 + ☐ = 45. Count up from 28 to 45 on the number line, or subtract: 45 − 28 = 17. Answer: 17 centimeters.

items.q: A paper chain was 36 feet long. The class made it longer. Now it is 62 feet long. How many feet did they add?
items.e: The change is unknown: 36 + ☐ = 62. Count up from 36 to 62 on the number line, or subtract: 62 − 36 = 26. Answer: 26 feet.

items.q: A rope was 80 centimeters long. Elijah cut some off. Now it is 53 centimeters long. How much did he cut off?
items.e: The change is unknown: 80 − ☐ = 53. Think: 53 + ☐ = 80. Subtract: 80 − 53 = 27. Answer: 27 centimeters.

items.q: Aaliyah has to walk 95 meters to the park. She has 68 meters left to go. How far has she walked so far?
items.e: The change is unknown: 95 − ☐ = 68. Think: 68 + ☐ = 95. Subtract: 95 − 68 = 27. Answer: 27 meters.

items.q: A rope was some feet long. Emma cut off 19 feet. Now it is 46 feet long. Which equation can you use to find how long it was at first?
items.e: The start is unknown, and 19 feet were cut off: ☐ − 19 = 46. Answer: 46 + 19 = 65 feet.

items.q: A tower was 34 centimeters tall. Gabriel added some blocks. Now it is 61 centimeters tall. Which equation can you use to find how much taller it got?
items.e: The tower got taller by an unknown amount: 34 + ☐ = 61. Answer: 61 − 34 = 27 centimeters.

items.q: A ribbon was 72 inches long. Jayden cut off some. Now it is 45 inches long. Which equation can you use to find how much was cut off?
items.e: An unknown length was cut off: 72 − ☐ = 45. Answer: 72 − 45 = 27 inches.

items.q: A sunflower grew 17 inches. Now it is 58 inches tall. Which equation can you use to find how tall it was before?
items.e: The start is unknown, and it grew 17 inches: ☐ + 17 = 58. Answer: 58 − 17 = 41 inches.

items.q: A board is 90 inches long. Valeria saws off 25 inches. Then she saws off 32 more inches. How long is the board now?
items.e: Step 1: First cut: 90 − 25 = 65. Step 2: Second cut: 65 − 32 = 33. Equation: 90 − 25 − 32 = ☐. Answer: 33 inches.

items.q: Nevaeh's block tower is 36 centimeters tall. Isaac's tower is 15 centimeters taller. Isaac puts his tower on top of Nevaeh's tower. How tall is the new tower?
items.e: Step 1: Isaac's tower: 36 + 15 = 51. Step 2: Together: 36 + 51 = 87. Equation: 36 + 36 + 15 = ☐. Answer: 87 centimeters.

items.q: A path is 80 meters long. The class walked 26 meters. Then they walked 35 more meters. How much farther is it to the end of the path?
items.e: Step 1: Walked: 26 + 35 = 61. Step 2: Still to go: 80 − 61 = 19. Equation: 80 − 26 − 35 = ☐. Answer: 19 meters.

items.q: Zoe has a red ribbon 34 centimeters long. Her blue ribbon is 18 centimeters longer. She tapes them end to end. How long is the new ribbon?
items.e: Step 1: Blue ribbon: 34 + 18 = 52. Step 2: Both: 34 + 52 = 86. Equation: 34 + 34 + 18 = ☐. Answer: 86 centimeters.

items.q: A fence will be 60 feet long. Workers built 23 feet on Monday and 19 feet on Tuesday. How many more feet do they need to build?
items.e: Step 1: Built: 23 + 19 = 42. Step 2: Still to build: 60 − 42 = 18. Equation: 60 − 23 − 19 = ☐. Answer: 18 feet.

items.q: A sunflower was 25 inches tall. It grew 12 inches in June and 16 inches in July. How tall is it now?
items.e: Step 1: June: 25 + 12 = 37. Step 2: July: 37 + 16 = 53. Equation: 25 + 12 + 16 = ☐. Answer: 53 inches.

items.q: A rope is 75 centimeters long. Sofia cuts off a piece 24 centimeters long and a piece 18 centimeters long. How much rope is left?
items.e: Step 1: Cut off: 24 + 18 = 42. Step 2: Left: 75 − 42 = 33. Equation: 75 − 24 − 18 = ☐. Answer: 33 centimeters.

items.q: Liam is 47 inches tall. He stands on a box that is 15 inches tall. A door is 84 inches tall. How much taller is the door than Liam on the box?
items.e: Step 1: Liam on the box: 47 + 15 = 62. Step 2: Difference: 84 − 62 = 22. Equation: 84 − 47 − 15 = ☐. Answer: 22 inches.

items.q: A race is 100 meters long. Grace ran 45 meters. Then she walked 28 meters. How much farther does she have to go?
items.e: Step 1: So far: 45 + 28 = 73. Step 2: Still to go: 100 − 73 = 27. Equation: 100 − 45 − 28 = ☐. Answer: 27 meters.

items.q: Marcus jumped 38 inches. Carlos jumped 9 inches farther than Marcus. Josiah's jump was 6 inches shorter than Carlos's. How far did Josiah jump?
items.e: Step 1: Carlos: 38 + 9 = 47. Step 2: Josiah: 47 − 6 = 41. Equation: 38 + 9 − 6 = ☐. Answer: 41 inches.
